stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.5 Instant as ChatGPT's Default Model, Claims 52% Fewer Hallucinations

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.5 Instant replaces GPT-5.3 Instant as ChatGPT's default model, rolling out to all users starting May 5
key_facts.excerpt: We're updating ChatGPT's default model, available to everyone, to be smarter and more accurate, with clearer, more concise answers that feel better tailored to you.

key_facts.fact: In internal evaluations, GPT-5.5 Instant produced 52.5% fewer hallucinated claims than GPT-5.3 Instant on high-stakes prompts in medicine, law, and finance
key_facts.excerpt: GPT‑5.5 Instant produced 52.5% fewer hallucinated claims than GPT‑5.3 Instant on high-stakes prompts covering areas like medicine, law, and finance.

key_facts.fact: The model reduced inaccurate claims by 37.3% on especially challenging conversations users had flagged for factual errors
key_facts.excerpt: It also reduced inaccurate claims by 37.3% on especially challenging conversations users had flagged for factual errors.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.5 Instant scored 81.2 on the AIME 2025 math test vs 65.4 for GPT-5.3 Instant, and 76 vs 69.2 on MMMU-Pro multimodal reasoning
key_facts.excerpt: The new model also achieved a score of 81.2 in the AIME 2025 math test, compared to 65.4 for the older model. It also outperformed its predecessor on the MMMU-Pro multimodal reasoning benchmark, with a score of 76 vs. 69.2.

key_facts.fact: Enhanced personalization uses past chats, files, and connected Gmail to tailor responses; rolling out first to Plus and Pro users on web
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT is now 'more effective' at pulling in context from things like previous chats and your Gmail to give you more personalized responses. This is a feature that Google is investing heavily in for Gemini as well.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.3 Instant will remain available for paid users for three months before being retired; the model is also available via API as 'gpt-5.5-chat-latest'
key_facts.excerpt: For developers, the GPT-5.5 model will be available through API as 'chat-latest,' with 5.3 available as an option for paid users for only three months.

stories.headline: Anthropic Commits to Spending $200B on Google Cloud and Chips Over Five Years

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has committed to spend $200 billion with Google Cloud over five years as part of a recent agreement, according to The Information
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has committed to spend US$200 billion with Google Cloud over five years as part of a recent agreement, The Information reported on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The commitment accounts for more than 40% of the revenue backlog Google disclosed to investors last week
key_facts.excerpt: The commitment suggests the artificial intelligence startup accounts for more than 40 per cent of the revenue backlog Google disclosed to investors last week.

key_facts.fact: Contracts from Anthropic and OpenAI now account for more than half of the $2 trillion in backlogs at major cloud providers including AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud
key_facts.excerpt: Contracts involving Anthropic and OpenAI now account for more than half of the US$2 trillion in backlogs at major cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a deal in April with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity expected online starting 2027; Broadcom's SEC filing cited approximately 3.5 GW
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom's SEC filing then put a harder number on the later phase: approximately 3.5 gigawatts of TPU-based AI compute capacity beginning in 2027, with Google and Broadcom agreements running through up to 2031.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet is also investing up to $40 billion in Anthropic, deepening its partnership with the AI startup
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet is also investing up to US$40 billion in Anthropic, deepening its partnership with the AI startup.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet is on the cusp of overtaking Nvidia as the world's most valuable company; the gap narrowed to ~$96 billion on May 5
key_facts.excerpt: FinanceCharts' Top 10 market-cap table, last updated May 5, 2026, put Nvidia at $4.772 trillion and Alphabet at $4.676 trillion. The gap was about $96 billion.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Nears $45B Valuation as China's Big Fund Seeks to Lead First Fundraise

key_facts.fact: China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund (the 'Big Fund') is in talks to lead DeepSeek's first-ever fundraising round at a ~$45 billion valuation
key_facts.excerpt: China's biggest state-backed semiconductor investment vehicle, China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund, is in talks to lead the financing of DeepSeek's first fundraising that could value the frontier AI lab at about $45 billion.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's valuation has surged from ~$20 billion expected just weeks earlier when fundraising talks began
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek's valuation has increased significantly in just a few weeks, up from the $20 billion expected when it started fundraising talks earlier.

key_facts.fact: Other investors still in talks include Tencent and Alibaba; founder Liang Wenfeng may also invest personal funds in the round
key_facts.excerpt: Other investors still in talks for a stake include Chinese tech giants Tencent and Alibaba. Liang could also invest his personal funds in this round.

key_facts.fact: The Big Fund has previously backed SMIC and Yangtze Memory Technologies but has not publicly backed any LLM developer before
key_facts.excerpt: The Big Fund has previously provided crucial financial support mainly to key manufacturing players in China's semiconductor industry, such as SMIC and Yangtze Memory Technologies. Notably, the state fund has not publicly backed any of China's large language model developers before.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek has never raised external funding before; founder Liang Wenfeng currently controls the company through personal holdings and affiliated entities
key_facts.excerpt: The Hangzhou-based startup was founded by billionaire Liang Wenfeng, who currently controls the company through personal holdings and affiliated entities.

stories.headline: Google Tests 'Remy' 24/7 AI Agent for Gemini, Quietly Shuts Down Project Mariner

key_facts.fact: Google is internally testing an AI agent codenamed 'Remy' that runs in a staff-only version of the Gemini app and integrates with Google services
key_facts.excerpt: Remy is your 24/7 personal agent for work, school, and daily life, powered by Gemini. It elevates the Gemini app into a true assistant that can take actions on your behalf — not just answer questions or generate content.

key_facts.fact: Remy can monitor things that matter to users, handle complex tasks proactively, and learn preferences over time, positioning it as Google's answer to OpenClaw
key_facts.excerpt: Deeply integrated across Google, Remy can monitor for things that matter to you, handle complex tasks proactively, and learn your preferences over time.

key_facts.fact: Google quietly shut down Project Mariner on May 5, the Chrome-browsing AI agent it highlighted onstage at I/O 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Google quietly shut down Project Mariner yesterday, the web-browsing AI agent it highlighted onstage last year at Google IO.

key_facts.fact: Google had previously moved staffers off the Project Mariner team as it pivoted toward OpenClaw-style agents, per WIRED reporting from ~2 months earlier
key_facts.excerpt: I reported for WIRED, nearly 2 months ago, that Google had moved staffers off the Project Mariner team as it responded to OpenClaw-style agents.

key_facts.fact: Google's I/O event is scheduled for May 19-20, where agents are expected to be a major focus; CEO Demis Hassabis has long outlined a vision for building a digital assistant
key_facts.excerpt: Google's upcoming I/O event later this month could be the stage for Remy's debut. Demis Hassabis has previously outlined plans to build advanced digital assistants.

stories.headline: Meta Builds OpenClaw-Inspired 'Hatch' AI Agent, Plans Instagram Shopping Tool Before Q4

key_facts.fact: Meta is developing a consumer AI agent internally codenamed 'Hatch,' inspired by OpenClaw, targeting internal testing completion by end of June
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is training an internal AI agent codenamed 'Hatch,' inspired by OpenClaw, with the goal of completing internal testing by the end of June.

key_facts.fact: Hatch is currently powered by Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 models, but will switch to Meta's own Muse Spark model at launch
key_facts.excerpt: Hatch is being trained on Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 models, and is expected to switch to Meta's latest model, Muse Spark, at launch.

key_facts.fact: Meta built virtual environments modeled on real websites like DoorDash, Etsy, and Reddit to safely test Hatch's capabilities
key_facts.excerpt: It has built virtual environments modeled on real websites such as DoorDash, Etsy and Reddit to safely test Hatch.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Meta plans an agentic shopping tool for Instagram, targeting launch before Q4, to compete with TikTok Shop
key_facts.excerpt: Meta plans to integrate the separate agentic shopping tool into its Instagram service and is targeting a launch before the fourth quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: Meta raised its AI infrastructure capex this year to as much as $145 billion; CEO Zuckerberg said the goal is to 'build agents that understand your goals and work around the clock'
key_facts.excerpt: Zuckerberg stated that Meta's goal is to 'build agents that can understand your goals and work around the clock to help you achieve them.' Meta has already announced it is raising its AI infrastructure capital expenditure this year to as much as $145 billion.

key_facts.fact: Meta tried to acquire OpenClaw but was outbid by OpenAI; it also faces potential cancellation of its Manus acquisition after Chinese authorities intervened
key_facts.excerpt: Meta also attempted an acquisition, but it did not happen. Meta is in a situation where it may have to cancel a deal for Manus, an AI agent developed by a Chinese startup that it acquired in December last year, after Chinese government authorities put the brakes on it.

stories.headline: Apple to Let iOS 27 Users Choose Third-Party AI Models Across Writing Tools, Siri, and More

key_facts.fact: Apple plans to let users select from multiple third-party AI models for tasks like generating and editing text and images in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 this fall
key_facts.excerpt: Apple plans to let users pick from a lineup of third-party models when asking their devices to perform generative AI tasks. This change is planned to arrive in iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS 27.

key_facts.fact: The feature is internally called 'Extensions,' allowing users to access AI capabilities from installed apps through Siri, Writing Tools, Image Playground, and more
key_facts.excerpt: Extensions allow you to access generative AI capabilities from installed apps on demand, through Apple Intelligence features such as Siri, Writing Tools, Image Playground and more.

key_facts.fact: Apple has been internally testing integrations with at least Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, in addition to the existing ChatGPT integration
key_facts.excerpt: Those models will be tasked with answering queries, editing and generating text, and image generation. These integrations have apparently included models from Anthropic and Google.

key_facts.fact: Users will be able to assign different Siri voices when conversing with external AI models vs. in-house Siri
key_facts.excerpt: For Siri, users will be able to select a different voice for conversations that use external models. This is to make it easier for users to quickly understand which AI source is handling the query.

key_facts.fact: A dedicated App Store section will list compatible AI apps; providers opt in by adding compatibility through their App Store applications
key_facts.excerpt: AI companies that opt in and add support to their App Store programs will be available to power Apple's AI tools in what the company is internally calling Extensions.

stories.headline: Anthropic Releases 10 AI Agent Templates for Financial Services, From Pitch Decks to KYC

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released 10 ready-to-run agent templates for financial services tasks including building pitchbooks, KYC screening, earnings review, and month-end close
key_facts.excerpt: We're releasing ten ready-to-run agent templates for the most time-consuming work in financial services: building pitchbooks, screening KYC files, and closing the books at month-end.

key_facts.fact: Each agent template ships as a plugin in Claude Cowork and Claude Code, or as cookbooks for Claude Managed Agents, enabling deployment in days rather than months
key_facts.excerpt: Each one ships as a plugin in Claude Cowork and Claude Code, and as a cookbook for Claude Managed Agents, so a team can put Claude on real financial work in days rather than months.

key_facts.fact: Claude now works across Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook through new add-ins for Microsoft 365, with context carrying automatically between applications
key_facts.excerpt: Claude also now works across Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook through the Claude add-ins for Microsoft 365. Once the add-ins are installed, context carries automatically between applications.

key_facts.fact: Claude Opus 4.7 leads the industry on Vals AI's Finance Agent benchmark at 64.37%
key_facts.excerpt: These updates pair best with Claude Opus 4.7, which is state-of-the-art on financial tasks and leads the industry on Vals AI's Finance Agent benchmark, at 64.37%.

key_facts.fact: Financial services is Anthropic's second-highest revenue-contributing industry; the launch came one day after Anthropic's $1.5B joint venture with Blackstone and Goldman Sachs
key_facts.excerpt: The reveal of 10 agent templates for banks, asset managers, and insurers comes just after its announced $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, and other Wall Street heavy-hitters.

key_facts.fact: Customer deployments cited include AIG, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, IG Group, and Moody's
key_facts.excerpt: Customer stories from AIG, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, IG Group, and Moody's.
